text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Wednesday.

LONDON - The UK's FTSE 100 index ended modestly higher on Wednesday but worries over the strength of sterling, rises in corporate taxes and possible interest rate hikes here and in the U.S. continued to weigh on sentiment. The FTSE finished 7.8 points firmer at 4,294.6. A late surge in B.A.T Industries accounted for most of the rise.
FRANKFURT - German shares ended bourse trade on Wednesday at higher levels, reaping the benefits of a higher close on Wall Street overnight, but with sentiment muted by the weaker dollar.
The DAX-30 index of leading German shares ended 25.77 points higher at 3,353.45. In post-bourse trade the index fell 21.72 to 3,347.54.

PARIS - French stocks ended fractionally higher on Wednesday, helped by Wall Street's gains, but off their session highs as a stronger-than-expected U.S. industrial production data fanned fears of higher interest rates. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 0.34 point at 2,620.97.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended weaker on Wednesday after a session which saw prices fluctuate in a narrow range. Dealers said the market ran out of steam after a firm opening and turned lower when U.S. data signaled strong economic growth. The Broad SPI closed down 8.40 to 2,927.32.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended modestly higher on Wednesday as investors, encouraged by the yen's recent weakness, sought relatively low-priced shares that are sensitive to the economy.

But some high-priced blue chips were capped by profit-taking, limiting overall gains. A rebound in the long-strapped financial sector also provided relief to the market, brokers said. The 225-share Nikkei average climbed 97.61 points to close at 18,031.20.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks closed sharply higher on Wednesday, prompted by the jump by U.S. stocks and bonds on benign U.S. inflation report, brokers said. "There is a very strong correlation between the U.S. (long) bond market and Hong Kong, so the market is adjusting to the rally in bonds last night," said Gary Wong, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Hang Seng Index climbed 239.29 points to close at 12,581.31.
SYDNEY - The Australian share market gained one percent in steady trade on Wednesday after the Dow gained two percent on Tuesday following weaker than expected March U.S. CPI data.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index ended up 24.7 points at 2,406.4, near its intra-day high of 2,410.7.
JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares slid to the close on Wednesday after touching a four-year low as bullion sank under the $340 an ounce level.

Dealers said the metal price and the worrying prospect of very disappointing first quarter results were weighing the index, but they added that gold counters were holding their heads above water better than would be expected.

Bullion fixed $1.55 down at $339.90 on Wednesday afternoon, and was seen nearing its February 12 low of $336.15, the lowest in almost four years. Gold shares closed 17.8 points down at 1,252.6. Industrial shares closed 9.2 down at 8,228.3 points and the all-share index ended 20.5 points weaker at 6,976.8.
